newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SAFRICA BATSMEN PUMMEL WEAK INDIA A ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SAFRICA BATSMEN PUMMEL WEAK INDIA A ATTACK.

text.p: Openers Herschelle Gibbs and Brian McMillan shared a 313-run partnership on Thursday as South Africa went on the rampage against a weak India A selection.
All-rounder Lance Klusener joined in the run feast, hitting the third century in the visitors' second innings, as the three-day game ended in a draw.

The Gibbs-McMillan partnership was only 17 runs short of the record opening stand by South Africa in any first class match abroad, the 330 runs scored by Bruce Mitchell (195) and Eric Rowan (171) in 1934 against Surrey at The Oval.
Gibbs, following up his career best 200 not out in the first innings, thumped 21 fours and three sixes in his 171 before holing out to Ajay Jadeja off the bowling of skipper W.V. Raman.
McMillan, an all-rounder who has been having a lean time with the bat on the current tour, hit a fluent 130 with 16 fours before getting out.
Klusener made 102 not out in 87 balls, including four sixes and 11 fours.
The visitors opted to bat the whole day, ending the final session at 492 for three wickets giving South Africa much-needed practice before the third test starting on Sunday. The series is tied 1-1.

Gibbs is the second South African on the current tour to score two centuries in the same match. Last Saturday, opener Gary Kirsten scored centuries in each innings as South Africa cruised to an easy 329-run win over India in the second test.
